title: Anyone willing to reap is called, if humble and loving
setting: Joseph Knight Sr. was a farmer and miller from Colesville, New York. He had helped Joseph Smith with food, money, and paper since 1827. In May 1829 Joseph and Oliver Cowdery ran short of supplies at Harmony, Pennsylvania. Knight soon came to Harmony with paper and enough food to finish the translation. Joseph’s history says Knight was anxious to know his duty, so Joseph asked the Lord for him. The exact day of Knight’s arrival is not recorded.
summary: The revelation opens by announcing that a great and marvelous work is about to come forth. The voice speaks as God and calls its word sharper than a two-edged sword. It says the field is ready for harvest, and whoever reaps with might is called of God. It promises that those who ask will receive. Because Knight has asked, it tells him to keep the commandments and help establish the cause of Zion. It then says no one can assist unless humble, loving, faithful, hopeful, charitable, and temperate. It closes with the speaker naming himself the light and life of the world.

contextNote.title: Who may help with the work
contextNote.text: Knight was not a scribe or a translator, so his place in the work was unclear. Verse 8 answers by naming the qualities a helper needs, not a skill or an office. Humility and love come first, then faith, hope, and charity. The list ends with temperance in “all things” entrusted to the helper’s care. Verse 6 had already given Knight a task: help bring forth the cause of Zion. Read together, the two verses say the task is open, but the character is required. In this passage, to “assist” means to support the work with a disciplined and loving life.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 teaches that each person can take part in God’s “great and marvelous work.” Verse 8 lists the qualities required to assist; which one did Knight show by bringing supplies, and which one could you work on?
reviewNote: Read all 9 verses. Official heading gives Harmony, May 1829, to Joseph Knight Sr., at his request. JSP historical introduction read for Knight’s background, his supply trip, and the uncertain arrival date. JSP notes this revelation may have come shortly after D&C 11. Verses 1–5 closely repeat D&C 4 and 11. Fact-check 2026-10-12: ldsText overstated the CFM lesson (it only briefly mentions Knight); now names the lesson’s actual teaching. reviewNote corrected: JSP says shortly after D&C 11, not before.
